title: A phone-provisioning endpoint that speaks XML to trusted peers concatenates one of its fields into a superuser SQL statement
index_line: T-0073 · EXEC · unauthenticated /pa XML notification: PhoneIP → PostgreSQL concat → COPY TO PROGRAM → RCE · perl · corroborated
invariant_violated: The notification endpoint assumed that anything able to POST a PolycomIPPhone document was another phone system already inside the trust boundary, so the PhoneIP field was handled as a validated address rather than as text that reaches a SQL parser — one that runs as the database superuser.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated POST to /pa carries an XML body beginning <PolycomIPPhone> naming a notification target
PhoneAppsHandler.pm parses the body with XML::Simple::XMLin and pulls PhoneIP out of the resulting structure without validation
PhoneIP is spliced into a single-quoted SQL predicate (auto_phone_config WHERE ip_address = '<PhoneIP>')
the statement runs through the application's PostgreSQL handle, which connects as the database superuser
injected SQL extends the statement with COPY (…) TO PROGRAM, so the database server itself evaluates an OS command
the command runs as the database server's OS user, giving unauthenticated remote code execution

source.http.body.value: an unauthenticated POST to /pa carrying a PolycomIPPhone XML document (the IP-phone notification protocol)

sink.sql.concat.value: PhoneIP concatenated into the single-quoted ip_address predicate, then executed by the app's PostgreSQL handle

sink.exec.shell.value: PostgreSQL COPY … TO PROGRAM evaluates a shell command as the database server's OS user — the SQL grammar is the shell door

guard.none.value: no authentication on /pa, no caller allowlist, and no parameterisation of the query

preconditions.expr: the /pa endpoint answers without a session
the tree contains the phone-notification handler that parses XML and concatenates a field into SQL
the application's database role can run COPY … TO PROGRAM (superuser or pg_execute_server_program member)

check.spec: psql "$APP_DSN" -tAc "SELECT rolsuper OR pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_execute_server_program','member') FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user"

success: a boolean/UNION probe returns data that exists only in the database
the injected COPY … TO PROGRAM spawns a process: an outbound connection to the tester, or command output written to a web-served path
failure_like: /pa answers 404/403 or demands authentication before parsing
PhoneIP is parameterised or matched against an address allowlist, so quotes are data
false_positive: a 200 response to a well-formed XML body is reachability, not injection — require a database-derived difference (error text naming the predicate, or a value only the DB knows)
a generic 500 on malformed XML proves the parser ran, not that the field reached the query

hazards: any machine-to-machine endpoint that parses XML from a peer protocol (phones, printers, PBX, monitoring agents) and reuses a field in SQL
the DB role matters more than the injection: a superuser handle turns a plain SQLi into file read/write and shell
the field looks like an IP address to every reviewer, which is why it survives code review
non_transfers: database roles limited to DML on one schema with no pg_execute_server_program membership

evidence.target: Sangoma Switchvox SMB 8.3 (104997), unauthenticated /pa phone-notification endpoint (CVE-2026-9586)

provenance.author: SRA Labs (labs.sra.io)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-9586: the unauthenticated /pa endpoint parses a <PolycomIPPhone> XML body and concatenates the attacker-controlled PhoneIP value directly into PostgreSQL queries without parameterisation (CWE-89)

provenance.author: Horizon3.ai Attack Research Team
provenance.corroborates: source-level trace of the same mechanism in PhoneAppsHandler.pm::tel_notify: XML::Simple::XMLin at line 180, PhoneIP taken unvalidated at 199/210, concatenated at 220-225, executed as PostgreSQL superuser at 226 with COPY ... TO PROGRAM
